newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil quiet, but not finished yet.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil quiet, but not finished yet.

text.p: NWE cracked fuel oil drifted sideways on Thursday in a quiet market.
A 45-50,000 tonne low sulphur cracked cargo was rumoured to have been sold out of Scandinavia, but details on prices were not forthcoming.
"Its the best kept secret of the day," commented one trader at a major.
"Its still unclear, some people think it went fixed, others that it was done at low quotes," said another.
There were also rumours that a smaller handysize cargo was done ex-France.
Traders said that with little concrete evidence to suggest otherwise wet low sulphur barrels were pegged around $127 fob NWE.
The high sulphur cracked market was very quiet amid a lack of pressure from both sellers and buyers. Material was available to meet limited demand.
"No one is taking positions, its just bits and bobs," said one trader who pegged prices steady around $115 cif.
High sulphur barges regained some lustre moving up to $119 fob ARA a tonne amid fairly good shipper demand.
